findings.title: The Charton et al. framing ignores the repository's own reading: the space matches B_21, and Table 3 is the draft's working datum

findings.quote: result. We have not checked that their space coincides with ours beyond its
findings.claim: Within V_21, 'a space of the size the authors use', Lemma 9.1's caps cannot give 4.00438. This 'locates an inconsistency in the draft', and the note has not checked that their space coincides with ours beyond its dimension.
findings.issue: (a) The hedge contradicts the repository's own literature reading. notes/stadlmann-recheck-s5.md ('Basis and dimension (Section 11, p. 42): CONFIRMED') quotes [Cha26]: 'B21 = spanQ {(L - P1)^a P_lambda : a >= 0, lambda_j in 2Z>0, a + |lambda| <= 21}', with P_lambda a product of power sums. Lemma 9.1 says 'the dilation sends the two physical rough caps to C(1) = C(2) = 31/50 and C(s) = 17/25'. Without this, a reader cannot tell whether the inconsistency touches which caps the analytic part justifies, which is the question that decides whether the 212 claim is at risk.

findings.title: AI-assistance statement and 'independent programs' understate how the work was produced
findings.quote: Prepared with the assistance of Claude (Anthropic).
findings.claim: The note was prepared with AI assistance. capped_check.py 'was written separately from the definitions only, without access to the first program'.
findings.issue: Per STATE.md and log/entries.json, both evaluators, the Song-Yue scripts, the Lean files, the text and the 'internal referee report' were produced by AI agents. capped_check.py was written by a 'helper' agent and capped_exact.py by the session agent. 'Independent' therefore means separate AI contexts working from the same definitions, not separate human authors. An expert reader weighing two-program agreement should know this: errors common to the shared transcription of the definitions, such as the one-band J_T of main.tex:155-157, are not caught by such agreement. The one-line \thanks does not say what the assistance covered. For a public posting (e.g. arXiv, whose policy holds authors responsible for AI-generated content) this matters more than in the repository.
findings.evidence: STATE.md Session 6 ('capped_exact.py (mine ...) and code/capped_check.py (helper, independent ...)'); log/entries.json line 64 ('A fresh-context helper audited the four new scripts').
findings.analysis: Per STATE.md and log/entries.json, both evaluators, the Song-Yue scripts, the Lean files, the text and the 'internal referee report' were produced by AI agents. capped_check.py was written by a 'helper' agent and capped_exact.py by the session agent. 'Independent' therefore means separate AI contexts working from the same definitions, not separate human authors. An expert reader weighing two-program agreement should know this: errors common to the shared transcription of the definitions, such as the one-band J_T of main.tex:155-157, are not caught by such agreement. The one-line \thanks does not say what the assistance covered. For a public posting (e.g. arXiv, whose policy holds authors responsible for AI-generated content) this matters more than in the repository. Evidence: STATE.md Session 6 ('capped_exact.py (mine ...) and code/capped_check.py (helper, independent ...)'); log/entries.json line 64 ('A fresh-context helper audited the four new scripts').
findings.suggested_fix: Expand the statement: say which parts (programs, Lean, text, internal referee) were produced by AI agents under the author's direction, that 'independent' means separate agent contexts without access to each other's code, and that both programs share the note's transcription of the definitions. Add one sentence to Method saying what two-program agreement does and does not rule out.

An expert who wants to judge what the programs compute needs three things: (i) why the transcribed one-band J_T is the criterion of [Sta26, Prop. 1]; (ii) the decomposition into pieces (indexed by m and j) and the two radial variables (r_A, rho); (iii) how capped_check.py's direct sum over exact large sets works. The note gives one dense sentence (main.tex:233-237) and otherwise points to a website document whose content can change. The paragraph at main.tex:233-249 then mixes this reduction with Lean ranges and a caveat about non-admissible bases, with no stated strategy. This is a residual of the earlier run's N011, which v0.2 did not fully resolve.

findings.title: Version history is woven into the mathematical text, and the changelog is internal-facing
findings.claim: Paragraph headings and sentences carry version tags ('(version 0.3)', '(version 0.4)'), and a four-entry changelog cites an internal referee report directory.
findings.issue: For a reader of a posted note, it does not matter when a result was confirmed, only which evidence it has. The sentence 'Proposition~\ref{prop:kin-own} below is also confirmed by both programs (version 0.4)' sits in the witness paragraph before the proposition is stated, which forces a forward reference. The Changes section (the 0.2 entry alone is 17 lines of internal fixes, plus 'in the directory \texttt{referee/} of the repository') belongs in the repository history. The paper's evidence labels already carry the current status.
findings.analysis: For a reader of a posted note, it does not matter when a result was confirmed, only which evidence it has. The sentence 'Proposition~\ref{prop:kin-own} below is also confirmed by both programs (version 0.4)' sits in the witness paragraph before the proposition is stated, which forces a forward reference. The Changes section (the 0.2 entry alone is 17 lines of internal fixes, plus 'in the directory \texttt{referee/} of the repository') belongs in the repository history. The paper's evidence labels already carry the current status. Evidence: main.tex:390, 401-402, 521-550.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the version tags from the body. Retitle the paragraph 'Second program', and move the kin-own sentence after Prop. prop:kin-own (where main.tex:410-412 already says it). For posting, replace the Changes section with a one-line pointer to the repository's changelog at the tagged release.

findings.title: The 236 results are hard to read: four ratios in two normalisations with mixed provenance in one theorem item and a cryptic table cell
findings.location: Results table main.tex:108-109; Thm thm:sy item (3) main.tex:365-369
findings.claim: Status 'Computed, two programs' with the sub-cell '($J_T$; $I_T$ one)'; the theorem is titled 'items (1) and (2) each by two independent programs'.
findings.issue: Item (3) lists 48J_T/I_0 (SY normalisation and Polymath), 48J_T/I_T and 48J_0/I_0. These have different evidence: J_T, I_0 and J_0 have two programs each, while I_T has one. The provenance of I_T is stated only after the theorem (main.tex:399-400), and the table compresses it into '($J_T$; $I_T$ one)', which a reader must decode. Under the heading 'two programs', 4.0030988 rests on a one-program I_T. The information is all present, but it costs a re-read.
findings.analysis: Item (3) lists 48J_T/I_0 (SY normalisation and Polymath), 48J_T/I_T and 48J_0/I_0. These have different evidence: J_T, I_0 and J_0 have two programs each, while I_T has one. The provenance of I_T is stated only after the theorem (main.tex:399-400), and the table compresses it into '($J_T$; $I_T$ one)', which a reader must decode. Under the heading 'two programs', 4.0030988 rests on a one-program I_T. The information is all present, but it costs a re-read. Evidence: main.tex:108-109, 357-370, 399-400.
findings.suggested_fix: Give the 236 witness a four-row mini-table (quantity, value in Polymath scaling, value in SY normalisation, programs), or split the table row in two: '48J_T/I_0 = 4.0026597 (SY criterion), two programs' and '48J_T/I_T = 4.0030988, I_T one program'. In item (3), add '(I_T by one program)'.

findings.title: 'Cap-free optimiser' is defined as an eigenvector, but the exact values refer to an unstated rational approximation
findings.location: Method main.tex:257-258; Thm thm:240 (1) main.tex:302-303; Prop. prop:212 main.tex:429-432
findings.quote: A ``cap-free optimiser of degree $D$'' is the top generalised
findings.claim: A cap-free optimiser of degree D is the top generalised eigenvector of (kJ_0, I_0) on V_D. Thm 240(1): 'for P the cap-free optimiser in V_20 ... = 4.0120389035...'.
findings.issue: The top generalised eigenvector of two rational matrices is in general irrational and is defined only up to scale. The evaluators take 'a polynomial P with rational coefficients' (main.tex:261). The exact values in Thm thm:240 (1) and Prop. prop:212 therefore belong to a particular rational vector (e.g. code/cap6/P_capfree_D20_u.json, rational coefficients taken from code/cert_stad49_capfree_D20e.json), not to the eigenvector. Thm thm:240 (2) and Prop. prop:kin-own state their rounding ('400 significant bits'), but (1) and prop:212 do not. The ten printed digits are reproducible only from the file.
findings.evidence: code/cap6/P_capfree_D20_u.json ('source': 'code/cert_stad49_capfree_D20e.json', coefficients are long exact fractions); main.tex:261, 302-306, 405-406, 429-432.
findings.analysis: The top generalised eigenvector of two rational matrices is in general irrational and is defined only up to scale. The evaluators take 'a polynomial P with rational coefficients' (main.tex:261). The exact values in Thm thm:240 (1) and Prop. prop:212 therefore belong to a particular rational vector (e.g. code/cap6/P_capfree_D20_u.json, rational coefficients taken from code/cert_stad49_capfree_D20e.json), not to the eigenvector. Thm thm:240 (2) and Prop. prop:kin-own state their rounding ('400 significant bits'), but (1) and prop:212 do not. The ten printed digits are reproducible only from the file. Evidence: code/cap6/P_capfree_D20_u.json ('source': 'code/cert_stad49_capfree_D20e.json', coefficients are long exact fractions); main.tex:261, 302-306, 405-406, 429-432.
findings.suggested_fix: Define the cap-free optimiser as 'the rational vector of the certificate file X, an approximation of the top generalised eigenvector', or state the rounding rule in Thm thm:240 (1) and Prop. prop:212 as in (2). Name the input file of each exact value in Reproducibility.

findings.title: The status-label system drifts: 'Computed' is defined as exact but used for ball and interval results, and 'conditional' is an undeclared label
findings.location: Introduction main.tex:95-98; Prop. prop:ceiling main.tex:441; main.tex:317-318; Corollaries main.tex:321, 417
findings.quote: \lbl{Computed} (exact certificate and a script that reproduces it),
findings.claim: Labels: Computed (exact certificate and script), Proved here, Lean-checked, Literature, Claimed.
findings.issue: Prop. prop:ceiling is labelled '\lbl{Computed}, ball arithmetic' and the 4.14 ceiling '(\lbl{Computed}, interval arithmetic ...)'. Neither is an exact certificate in the sense of the definition. The corollaries use a sixth label, 'conditional; the analytic input is \lbl{Claimed}', and Remark rem:lemma5 uses '\lbl{Literature} reading, not a result'. Changing the qualifier on the same label (exact / ball / interval; one or two programs) is reasonable, but the declared definition should cover it.
findings.analysis: Prop. prop:ceiling is labelled '\lbl{Computed}, ball arithmetic' and the 4.14 ceiling '(\lbl{Computed}, interval arithmetic ...)'. Neither is an exact certificate in the sense of the definition. The corollaries use a sixth label, 'conditional; the analytic input is \lbl{Claimed}', and Remark rem:lemma5 uses '\lbl{Literature} reading, not a result'. Changing the qualifier on the same label (exact / ball / interval; one or two programs) is reasonable, but the declared definition should cover it. Evidence: main.tex:96-98, 299, 317-318, 321, 357, 404, 417, 428, 441, 465.
findings.suggested_fix: Redefine Computed as 'machine computation with a script that reproduces it, in exact rational or rigorous ball/interval arithmetic as stated', with 'two programs' as a declared qualifier, and declare 'conditional' as the label for corollaries whose hypotheses include Claimed inputs.

findings.title: Song-Yue notation block: J versus J_T, an incompletely defined star, and SY's own L versus the note's L
findings.quote: on $\{\sum_it_i<U_{\mathrm{SY}}\}$, $J$ the capped numerator, both in their
findings.claim: Here I_0 is the cap-free mass, J the capped numerator, and the stars denote integer coordinates x=10^4 t. Their criterion is 48J/I_0>2001/2000.
findings.issue: (a) The note's own convention is J_0 for cap-free and J_T for capped (main.tex:152-159). The SY block uses bare J for the capped numerator (main.tex:131, 342-343) and then J_T in Thm thm:sy, so one object has two names. (b) 'the stars denote integer coordinates $x=10^4t$' does not match Thm thm:sy (1)-(2). There the factors 5^150 521^50 come from also scaling the polynomial by 65125^25, which is explained only 30 lines later (main.tex:373-376). A reader checking I_ref=(98!)^2 I_0^* against item (1) first finds a mismatch. (c) In [SY26], L = A - eps = 491/2000 is the marginal parameter (notes/sources-236-song-yue.md line 13). In the note, L is the support length (their U, times 4). The renaming to U_SY is done, but the clash with SY's L is not flagged for a reader comparing with the source.
findings.analysis: (a) The note's own convention is J_0 for cap-free and J_T for capped (main.tex:152-159). The SY block uses bare J for the capped numerator (main.tex:131, 342-343) and then J_T in Thm thm:sy, so one object has two names. (b) 'the stars denote integer coordinates $x=10^4t$' does not match Thm thm:sy (1)-(2). There the factors 5^150 521^50 come from also scaling the polynomial by 65125^25, which is explained only 30 lines later (main.tex:373-376). A reader checking I_ref=(98!)^2 I_0^* against item (1) first finds a mismatch. (c) In [SY26], L = A - eps = 491/2000 is the marginal parameter (notes/sources-236-song-yue.md line 13). In the note, L is the support length (their U, times 4). The renaming to U_SY is done, but the clash with SY's L is not flagged for a reader comparing with the source. Evidence: main.tex:131, 152-159, 339-348, 361-364, 373-376; notes/sources-236-song-yue.md:13.
findings.suggested_fix: Write J_T throughout the SY block. Define the star as 'x=10^4 t together with the integer rescaling of P by 65125^{25} of [SY26, Eq. (71)]' at first use. Add a parenthesis: '(their L=491/2000 is our tau/4)'.

findings.title: Minor overloading and an undefined norm: P, s, D and |u'|
findings.quote: Let $R=L-|u'|$ on the fibre over $u'\in\mathbb R^{k-1}_{\ge0}$, and call $u'$
findings.claim: R = L - |u'|; P_j power sums; P a test polynomial; s(u) the large-set mass; D the diameter and the degree.
findings.issue: |u'| (used in main.tex:203 and 215) is never defined. It means the coordinate sum, which the note writes u_1+...+u_k elsewhere. P_j (power sums, Lemma lem:egf) and P, P^*, P(z), P_SY (test polynomials) share a letter, so 'P_2,...,P_24' (power sums) sits next to 'P_SY' (a polynomial) at main.tex:353-354. s is the large-set mass s(u) (main.tex:146) and the formal variable of the generating function in Lemma lem:egf (main.tex:192). D is the tuple diameter in Section 1 (main.tex:67) and the degree of V_D in Section 3. None of these causes a real ambiguity in context, so each costs at most a moment.

P_j (power sums, Lemma lem:egf) and P, P^*, P(z), P_SY (test polynomials) share a letter, so 'P_2,...,P_24' (power sums) sits next to 'P_SY' (a polynomial) at main.tex:353-354. s is the large-set mass s(u) (main.tex:146) and the formal variable of the generating function in Lemma lem:egf (main.tex:192). Evidence: global search of full-source.tex for '|u', 'P_', 's^', 'D'.
findings.suggested_fix: Define |u|=u_1+...+u_k once, next to R_k. Rename the formal variable in Lemma lem:egf (e.g. z) and the diameter (e.g. diam H). Optionally write p_j for power sums.
